- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30% in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are volatile, model underestimates downside risk; add 10–20% buffer to lower end of forecast range.
- After sharp price spikes (true outcome > 3x recent mean), model often overshoots; cap 30d forecast at 2x recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.33, 1.00, 0.33), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average if sentiment shifts.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome exceeds 10x recent 18d average, model is likely overconfident; apply downward correction proportional to sentiment volatility (e.g., 20% if sentiment variance > 0.5).
- If sentiment is uniformly low and true outcome is rising, model underestimates momentum; increase forecast slope by 10–15% for next 7–14 days.
